title.value: Patient experience or patient satisfaction? A systematic review of child- and family-reported experience measures in pediatric surgery
title.justification: The paper focuses on a systematic review of child- and family-reported experience measures in pediatric surgery, as evident from the title.
title.quote: Patient experience or patient satisfaction? A systematic review of child- and family-reported experience measures in pediatric surgery

extractions.description: The paper reviews the use of Patient-Reported Experience Measures (PREMs) in pediatric surgery, highlighting the need for more rigorous, validated tools that involve patient and parent input in their development, contrasting with current practices which commonly use non-validated satisfaction surveys.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on patient experience and satisfaction measures in the context of pediatric surgery, which does not directly relate to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Although PROMs are increasingly used in pediatric surgery, PREMs are not yet in use, being typically substituted by satisfaction surveys. Significant efforts are needed to develop and implement PREMs in pediatric surgical care, in order to effectively capture children's and families' voices.

primary_category.justification: The paper's central focus is on healthcare methodology and not climate or sustainability.
primary_category.quote: The study objectives were to identify the instruments used, assess their characteristics, and identify areas in which the use of PREMs could be improved.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not touch on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes as secondary topics either.
secondary_categories.quote: None of the studies reviewed assessed patients and families after major congenital interventions, which constitute the most profound family experiences in our specialty.

primary_sub_category.justification: Since the primary category is 'N/A', there is also no relevant sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: A unique challenge in assessing patient experience in pediatric care is that it must be measured from the perspective of both the children and their parents.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There are no secondary sub-categories relevant as the paper does not relate to sustainability themes.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: PREMs measure patients’ perception of their experience with the healthcare received.

applications.value: A systematic review of Patient-Reported Experience Measures (PREMs) in pediatric surgery.
applications.justification: This is the main focus of the paper as it reviews existing tools used in pediatric surgery.
applications.quote: PREMs measure patients’ perception of their experience with the healthcare received.

new_primary_category.justification: No new category is needed as the paper does not relate to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_category.quote: Although PROMs are increasingly used in pediatric surgery, PREMs are not yet in use, being typically substituted by satisfaction surveys.

new_primary_sub_category.quote: The number of publications reporting both patient experience and satisfaction in pediatric surgery has increased in recent years but remains limited.
